question.problem:
A course grade is calculated by adding the results of a written test, oral test, and colloquium, contributing $50%$, $30%,$ and $20%,$ respectively to the final grade. 

The written test results are normally distributed with a mean of $64$ and a standard deviation of $8.$ The oral test results are normally distributed with a mean of $50$ and a standard deviation of $10$, while the results of the colloquium are normally distributed with a mean of $60$ and a standard deviation of $10.$ Find the probability that a randomly selected student achieves a grade greater than $70.$ You may assume that the scores on each test are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9713\,$ | $\,0.9719\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ | $\,0.9732\,$ | $\,0.9738\,$ |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9772\,$ | $\,0.9778\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ | $\,0.9788\,$ | $\,0.9793\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9821\,$ | $\,0.9826\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ | $\,0.9834\,$ | $\,0.9838\,$ |

current_example.problem:
A shop sells $2$ types of rice, Type $A$ and Type $B.$ The volume per packet for Type $A$ rice is normally distributed with a mean of $1$ liter and a variance of $0.01$ liters2, while the volume per packet for Type $B$ rice is normally distributed with a mean of $0.7$ liters and a variance of $0.02$ liters2. During cooking, it is known that Type $A$ rice quadruples in volume, while Type $B$ rice triples in volume.

If a single package of Type $A$ rice and $2$ packages of Type $B$ rice are randomly selected and cooked, what is the probability that the resulting rice volume is less than $8$ liters? You may assume that the volumes of rice in the packages are mutually independent. 

*Hint: A table of values of $\Phi(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\, 0.06 \,$ | $\, 0.07 \,$ | $\, 0.08 \,$ | $\, 0.09 \,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\, -0.3 \,$ | $\, 0.3594 \,$ | $\, 0.3557 \,$ | $\, 0.3520 \,$ | $\, 0.3483 \,$ |
| $\, -0.2 \,$ | $\, 0.3974 \,$ | $\, 0.3936 \,$ | $\, 0.3897 \,$ | $\, 0.3859 \,$ |
| $\, -0.1 \,$ | $\, 0.4364 \,$ | $\, 0.4325 \,$ | $\, 0.4286 \,$ | $\, 0.4247 \,$ |
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $X_1$ denote the volume of the Type $A$ rice package, and let $X_2$ and $X_3$ denote the volumes of the Type $B$ rice packages. Then, we have

$$
X_1\sim N(1, 0.01), \qquad X_2\sim N(0.7, 0.02), \qquad X_3\sim N(0.7, 0.02).
$$

Let the random variable $Y$ denote the total resulting volume of rice after cooking. Since the Type $A$ rice quadruples in volume, while the type $B$ rice triples in volume, we have

$$
Y= 4X_1+3X_2 + 3X_3.
$$

The random variable $Y$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =(4\cdot 1+3\cdot 0.7+3\cdot 0.7) \\  & =8.2 \\ \text{Var}[Y] & ={4}^{2}\cdot 0.01+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.02+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.02 \\  & =16\cdot 0.01+9\cdot 0.02+9\cdot 0.02 \\  & =0.52.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
Y \sim N(8.2, 0.52).
$$

In order to find $P(Y \lt 8),$ we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<8) & =P(Z<\frac{8-8.2}{\sqrt{0.52}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-0.28) \\  & =Φ(-0.28)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\Phi(-0.28)\approx 0.3897.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<8) & ≈Φ(-0.28) \\  & ≈0.3897.\end{aligned}
$$
